summary_en: GMO Financial Holdings raised its FY2026 dividend forecast to 68.60 yen per share (from 57.04 yen), with quarterly dividends of 20.23 yen for Q3 and Q4, reflecting stronger-than-expected nine-month earnings driven by improved FX and CFD trading revenues.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revised Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase) Based on Q3 FY2026 Consolidated Financial Results Summary
translation_en_brief:
GMO Financial Holdings revised its full-year FY2026 dividend forecast upward to 68.60 yen per share from the previously announced 57.04 yen per share. This represents an increase of 11.56 yen per share. Under the revision, the Q3 and Q4 dividends are each set at 20.23 yen per share (compared to the prior Q2 revised forecast of 14.45 yen), with the additional 5.78 yen from the Q3 upside distributed equally between Q3 and Q4 to ensure stable and consistent profit distribution.

The revision follows stronger-than-expected nine-month results. Operating revenue reached 44.5 billion yen, up 15.9% year-over-year, while operating profit increased 17.3% to 16.1 billion yen. Net income attributable to parent company shareholders rose 18.2% to 10.5 billion yen. The company's operating profit for the nine-month period reached a record high. Key drivers included a recovery in FX trading revenue in Q3 (aided by U.S.-Japan policy coordination and yen-weakness rhetoric), sustained outperformance in CFD trading revenue, and robust deposit management and margin trading revenues.

The company's dividend policy targets a payout ratio of 65% or more of earnings attributable to parent company shareholders, with a DOE (dividend payout ratio on consolidated equity) floor of 10%. Based on Q3's earnings, the 65% payout ratio calculation yielded 22.08 yen per share, well above the year's stated floor of 10.52 yen, enabling the upward revision. The Q4 dividend forecast will be finalized based on full-year earnings progress.
